posts.title: THE PULSE GALA 2015
posts.content:
The 2015 Pulse Gala is an annual fundraiser hosted by CRF to promote Cardiovascular health. Each year CRF invites renowned scholars to join them as an honored guess. In 2015 CRF invited one of the world’s most accomplished and respected public servants to be the honoree. Dr. Henry Kissinger, a renowned scholar, foreign policy advisor, and prolific author.

Pulse Gala is updated yearly for CRF Annual Foundraiser. As the Junior Front End Developer at CRF I had the honor of handling all components of developing this website from 2013 – 2016.

The Pulse Gala is 1-3 page bootstrap website hosted annually. This website has no database and as such is a standard static html website built with twitter bootstrap, Javascript, jQuery, a slider, forms processed through wufoo forms and a gallery.

At CRF I handled all the development of smaller websites and majority of all front end development at the company.

Visit this website >> www.pulsegala.org/2015

posts.title: Transcatheter Cardiovascular Therapeutics (TCT) 2015
posts.content:
The Transcatheter Cardiovascular Therapeutics (TCT) is an annual conference hosted by CRF focusing on the future of interventional cardiology. Each year CRF invites millions of medical professional and scholars to join them at TCT. In 2015 CRF invited special guest speakers Arnold Schwarzenegger and Carlo Ancelotti.

TCT is updated yearly for CRF Annual TCT Conference. As the Junior Front End Developer at CRF I worked along a team of designers and developers to develop the TCT materials each year. From 2013-2017 I was the front end developer at CRF. Each year I handled the development of 8 – 15 TCT related websites for conferences, sponsors, and partners. As well as the front end development of TCT Industry website, App features and various related interfaces. In addition to website development I handled the development of over 200 emails sent each year through Salesforce’s Pardot on behalf of CRF, TCT, sponsors, and partners.

The TCT website is a Joomla website built in bootstrap, jQuery, Javascript and just about any tool that accomplished the task. TCT website housed dynamic schedules built using various technologies including Ajax, Restful Api and Javascript.

At CRF I handled all the development of smaller websites, majority of all front end development at the company and all of the CRF publication emails.

posts.title: Ali HairStylist Website
posts.content:
Ali is a master hairstylist. Working as a stylist since 1968, Ali has crafted his skills at Astor Place Hairstylists as well as MOI, alongside his own barbershop that he operated back in Morocco. Ali has had the pleasure of working in some of the most well-known fashion shows and hairstyling competitions in the world. He was ranked in 5th place during the World Hairstyling Competition of 1982. He is also a member of many different hairstyling federations, organizations, and associations that deal with barbers.

I had the pleasure of designing and developing Ali’s first website while a student in College.

I handled the entire design and development of Ali’s entire website. The website was build in wordpress as a custom theme with a responsive layout. Responsive and adaptive techiques were still fairly new at the time I developed this website so I was very pleased to see the results.

Since then his website site has been rebranded however he is an exceptional hair stylist and if you were interested in learning more about him please visit his website at >> https://www.alihairstylist.net/

posts.title: I WRITE NY CHALLENGE
posts.content:
The I WRITE NY CHALLENGE is an initiative was created by The Know in partnership with the Writers Guild of America and other organizations to help to cultivate the next generation of writers, journalists and communicators.

For this I Write NY created both print and digital design were created. A unique design was developed to highlight I Write NY Challenge on The Knows website. The Know website is built in wordpress as a child theme of WordPress Twentynineteen theme using twitter bootstrap, Javascript, jQuery, and a form processed through wordpress plugins.

As a private consultant to The Know I handle all design and development for many of their projects including the I Write NY Challenge as the solo designer and developer. This project later expanded to re-development of the entire Know website. I have been working with The Know on various materials, designs and webdevelopment for 10+ years.

Visit this website >> theknowledgeproject.org/i-write-ny/

posts.content:
A customizable marketing bundle was created for independent Color Street nail artists. The original visual materials were designed in Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator, then rebuilt in Canva as editable templates.

The templates were developed to give independent consultants a polished set of branded marketing materials that could be easily personalized without professional design software. Users could update text, offers, contact information and promotional content while maintaining a consistent visual style.

The project combined graphic design, template development and brand implementation, adapting finished Adobe-based designs into an accessible and reusable marketing system for non-designers.

posts.title: COLORSTREET MARKETING BUNDLES
posts.content:
I created a customizable marketing bundle for independent Color Street nail artists. I designed the original visual materials in Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator, then rebuilt the finished designs in Canva as editable templates.

The goal was to give independent consultants a polished set of branded marketing materials they could easily personalize themselves without needing professional design software. I structured the Canva templates so users could update their own text, offers, contact information and promotional content while keeping the overall design consistent.

This project combined graphic design, template design and practical brand implementation, taking finished Adobe-based designs and adapting them into an accessible, reusable system for non-designers.

posts.title: FIVE NINE
posts.content:
Five Nine was expanding its product line into larger retail stores, including TJ Maxx, and wanted to establish a more professional and consistent brand presence across its products.

A coordinated collection of branded product materials was developed to create a cohesive retail presentation across the line. The designs established consistent typography, color, layout and visual branding so that the individual products would be recognizable as part of the same Five Nine collection while still allowing each item to retain its own identity.

All of the materials were designed and prepared in Adobe Illustrator for use across the company’s product packaging, labels and supporting retail materials.

posts.title: THE PARENTS CLUB OF WEST POINT WINTER BALL 2019
posts.client: The Parents Club of West Point
posts.content:
I developed a complete Gatsby-inspired visual identity and coordinated event package for the Parents Club of West Point Winter Ball 2019. The design was carried across the invitation suite, custom belly band and seal, RSVP and dinner-selection pieces, hotel and directions information, event materials, sponsorship pieces and email campaign.

I created the print and digital materials using Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop and InDesign, prepared the files for production, programmed and sent the event emails, and added the event information and supporting graphics to the PCWP website.

I also handled the physical production and fulfillment of the invitation package, including printing, assembling and wrapping the invitations, preparing the envelopes and mailing the finished pieces. The project combined event branding, graphic design, digital communication, print production and hands-on assembly into one cohesive campaign.

posts.title: THE PARENTS CLUB OF WEST POINT WINTER BALL 2018
posts.client: The Parents Club of West Point
posts.content:
The Parents Club of West Point Winter Ball 2018 required a coordinated visual identity that could be carried across the many print and digital materials used to promote and organize the annual event.

A complete event package was developed around the winter-themed design, including the invitation suite, save-the-date materials, custom belly band and tags, RSVP and dinner-selection cards, hotel and directions information, sponsorship and silent-auction materials, event program and additional on-site graphics. The individual pieces were designed to function together as one consistent event system while accommodating the different information and production requirements of each format.

The campaign also extended into digital communications through coordinated email materials developed for the event, creating a consistent visual presentation from the initial invitation through event promotion and supporting materials.

posts.title: DFW PRIVATE EDUCATION FAMILIES OF COLOR CONFERENCE 2018
posts.content:
Promotional and conference materials were developed for DFW Private Education’s 2018 Families of Color Conference across print, web, social media and on-site event applications.

The campaign included graphics for the DFW website, multiple social media profiles, partner-school outreach and web advertising placements in a range of required sizes and formats. A printed promotional postcard was also designed specifically to meet United States Postal Service mailing and production specifications for postal distribution.

The conference identity was extended into large-format and environmental materials, including retractable banners, branded conference tablecloths, conference banners, table signage and other supporting event graphics. The result was a coordinated visual system that could be adapted consistently across digital promotion, direct mail and the physical conference environment.

posts.title: THE PARENTS CLUB OF WEST POINT TASTE & TOUR 2018: PASSPORT TO THE HUDSON RIVER
posts.client: The Parents Club of West Point (PCWP)
posts.skills:
Graphic Design
Illustration
Map Illustration
Event Design
Print Design
Adobe Illustrator
Adobe Photoshop
Adobe InDesign
Adobe Creative Cloud
Print Production
Z-Fold Brochure Production
Project Coordination
posts.content:
Taste & Tour was a Parents Club of West Point event featuring the Passport to the Hudson River, a custom-designed map and promotional piece highlighting participating local businesses.

I developed the complete visual design and layout for the Passport, including the illustrated map, business listings, advertising spaces and sponsor placements. I coordinated with PCWP, the event planner and participating local businesses to organize business locations and advertising according to sponsorship level and incorporated that information into the map and overall design.

I created the project using Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop and InDesign, developing the map illustration, graphic elements, typography, advertising layouts and print-ready production files. The finished piece was designed as a Z-fold so that it folded down into the format and proportions of a passport.

I also handled the physical print production of the project, including printing and machine-folding the finished pieces.
